source_of_truth: hand-authored, offline, before any InvestigationRun exists for this incident
root_cause_explanation: orders.amount_cents is already in cents. stg_orders.sql divides by 100 twice, so mart_daily reports 1/100th of the real revenue. Source counts are steady at ~300/day; only the mart's reported value moved. This is a pipeline defect, not a business change.

repair_must_satisfy.description: Any accepted repair must remove exactly one of the two divide-by-100 conversions in the amount calculation for stg_orders.sql, and must not touch order_id, order_date, or row counts.
repair_must_satisfy.reference_patch_effect: amount_cents / 100.0 AS amount_usd — single conversion only
alternative_repairs_are_acceptable_if: the patch still divides amount_cents by 100 exactly once (not zero, not twice)
row counts before and after are identical
no column other than the amount is altered
repair_must_satisfy.validation_requirement: REPAIR is only correct if ValidationResult.accepted == true. A correct diagnosis with a rejected repair is a failure, not a partial success.

why_not_no_repair: The source system is unaffected (steady ~300/day); the mart's number is provably wrong relative to its own source, so doing nothing is not correct.
why_not_escalate: The decisive evidence (source count vs. mart count, and the transform's SQL) is fully reachable through get_schema and run_sql. Nothing is missing that would justify abstaining.

scoring_notes.root_cause_match: exact match on root_cause_id is sufficient for a pass; a semantically equivalent root_cause_summary describing the same double-conversion defect also passes if root_cause_id differs — route to the judge agent for that case, never auto-fail on id mismatch alone
scoring_notes.repair_match: exact match on repair_id is not required — route to the judge agent whenever repair_id or patch differs from the reference, using repair_must_satisfy as the standard the alternative must meet
